title: From Homemaker To Driving School Entrepreneur: How NBCFDC Support Empowered Wayanad Kerala Based OBC Ezhava Community Woman Mini Devi
body_text:
Access to affordable finance can enable women to turn practical ideas into sustainable enterprises. Timely credit support helps aspiring entrepreneurs overcome capital constraints, build livelihoods and create services that benefit their communities.
Mini Devi, a resident of Wayanad district in Kerala, has experienced this transformation through self-employment assistance provided by the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC) through the Kerala State Backward Classes Development Corporation (KSBCDC).
A member of the OBC Ezhava community, Mini Devi was a homemaker who depended on household income. She wanted to become financially independent and establish an enterprise of her own, but limited resources prevented her from taking the first step.
Mini Devi aspired to start a driving school that would offer a comfortable and supportive learning environment, particularly for women. She also wanted to help women acquire driving skills, improve their mobility and become more confident and self-reliant.
The principal barrier was economic. Establishing a driving school required capital to purchase a training vehicle and create suitable office and classroom facilities. Without sufficient savings or an independent income, Mini Devi was unable to make the necessary investment.
With the loan, Mini Devi purchased a training vehicle and established an office for her venture, Malanad Driving School. The support enabled her to create the essential infrastructure required to begin operations and serve learners in her area.
Mini Devi’s women-friendly approach provides learners with a supportive setting in which they can acquire driving skills with confidence and convenience.
Today, Mini Devi is a confident entrepreneur and the owner of a successful driving school. Her transition from homemaker to business owner has brought financial independence, greater self-confidence and a stronger role in her family and community.
Mini Devi’s journey demonstrates how affordable credit and institutional support can help women overcome economic barriers and build viable enterprises. Her success also extends beyond personal income by enabling other women to gain mobility, skills and independence.
Talking about impact of the support, Mini Devi said, “I received an individual self-employment loan of Rs 3 lakh from NBCFDC through KSBCDC in 2025 that proved a turning point to translate my entrepreneurial vision into reality. I now successfully manage the driving school with a special focus on training women learners. After receiving the loan, my income increased to approximately Rs 40,000 per month strengthening my financial position and reducing dependence on household income.”
Through determination and timely assistance from NBCFDC through KSBCDC, Mini Devi transformed her aspiration into a sustainable livelihood. Malanad Driving School stands as an inspiring example of women-led entrepreneurship and the wider social impact of targeted self-employment support.

enrichment.summary: PIB highlights the story of Mini Devi, an OBC Ezhava woman from Wayanad, Kerala, who used a Rs 3 lakh individual self-employment loan from the National Backward Classes Finance and Development Corporation (NBCFDC), routed through the Kerala State Backward Classes Development Corporation (KSBCDC), to start Malanad Driving School in 2025. The venture focuses on training women drivers and has increased her monthly income to about Rs 40,000, making her financially independent.
enrichment.context: NBCFDC is a central public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Social Justice & Empowerment that provides concessional credit to Other Backward Classes (OBCs) and Economically Backward Classes (EBCs) for self-employment and income-generating activities, channelling funds through State Channelising Agencies like KSBCDC. Such schemes aim to promote entrepreneurship, especially among women, within backward communities as a tool for social and economic empowerment. This release is a routine human-interest success story used by the ministry to showcase the on-ground impact of its credit-linked self-employment schemes, rather than announcing any new policy, scheme change, or data of broader significance.
